title: Probe weighting and signal fidelity stitch plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a lightweight plan for assigning probe weights, clarifying signal fidelity (how ‘trustworthy’ a metric/trace is for different investigations), and stitching those signals into dashboard tiles with ownership and cost-awareness. It is intended for the observability guild, dashboard owners, and SREs working on quantize/rollout telemetry.

Context and motivation:
- We have many probes (synthetic, canary, user-session sampling, KV-warmth, prefix-warm probes) producing overlapping signals. Operators are confused which panel to trust during rollouts and incidents.
- High-cardinality trace capture is expensive; we need a principled weighting and sampling policy that encodes fidelity vs cost tradeoffs.
- Dashboards should surface the most actionable signal first and indicate a confidence score (derived from probe weighting + sampling coverage).

Definitions (working):
- Probe: any synthetic or real instrumentation that surfaces a metric/trace (eg. canary probe, microprobe, session sampler).
- Signal fidelity: a unitless score (0..100) representing expected usefulness for root cause given current sampling/config; higher means more likely to reveal causality quickly.
- Weight: operational importance multiplier used in aggregated views (dashboards, alert routing).
- Coverage: fraction of user sessions/requests sampled by the probe over a 1h window.
- Cost factor: approximate monthly dollars for retaining associated traces/metrics at current settings.

Proposed scoring formula (simple baseline):
- fidelity_score = clamp( (coverage_score * schema_completeness) * freshness_multiplier * stability_penalty, 0, 100 )
  - coverage_score = min(coverage_pct * 100, 100) where coverage_pct in [0,1] over 1h window
  - schema_completeness = 0.5..1.0 depending on presence of session_id, tenant_id, model_id, kv_tags (manual mapping)
  - freshness_multiplier = 1 for probes with median latency <= 200ms, 0.8 for 200-500ms, 0.6 for >500ms
  - stability_penalty = 1 - min(noise_index, 0.4) where noise_index is rolling stdev/mean of metric over 24h

- weight = base_owner_priority * (1 + fidelity_score/100) * (1 - cost_sensitivity)
  - base_owner_priority: [1.0 (low), 1.2 (medium), 1.5 (high)] assigned by owner during onboarding
  - cost_sensitivity: 0..0.4 knob depending on budget label (high-budget -> 0, low-budget -> 0.4)

Metric definitions to include in panel metadata (when possible):
- token_path_latency_p50/p90/p99 (ms): time from request accept to first token emitted (server-side). Aggregation: per-request latency, then compute quantiles over 5m windows.
- kv_cache_hit_rate (pct): kv_hits / kv_lookups, computed per model-shard, 5m rollup.
- probe_coverage (pct): sampled_requests / total_requests per tenant per 1h window.
- trace_sample_rate (ratio): number of traces retained / total eligible traces, per model.
- probe_estimated_cost_per_100k: derived estimate (USD) using current retention and trace-size profiles.

Tracing guidance for weighted probes:
- High-fidelity probes (fidelity_score > 70): retain full spans and logs for 48h, include dense annotations (prompt snippets hashed, model-version tag, KV keys redacted hash).
- Medium-fidelity probes (40..70): store sampled spans with reduced annotations for 24h, persist only spans > 100ms or error flagged.
- Low-fidelity probes (<40): retain span id + basic timing metadata for 7d, no full payloads.
- Implement a dynamic fallback: when a rollout triggers a model-quality alert, temporarily bump affected probe sample rates to 'high-fidelity' for a 30m window per tenant.

Dashboard stitching rules (practical):
- Each dashboard tile must expose: metric name, owner, fidelity_score, last_updated, sample_rate, estimated_cost_label (low/medium/high).
- Ordering logic: tiles sorted by (weight desc) with manual pinning allowed.
- Color cues: fidelity_score < 40 -> amber icon + tooltip "low confidence: consider increasing probe coverage"; <20 -> red.
- Drilldown actions per tile: link to trace explorer filtered by session_id, link to probe config, open Jira template prefilled with metric and evidence.
- When showing aggregates across tenants, surface a coverage heatmap to show blindspots.

Ownership and runway (who does what):
- Owner role (per probe) is responsible for assigning base_owner_priority, validating schema_completeness, and keeping cost_sensitivity aligned with budget tag.
- Observability guild will:
  1) run a week-long audit to compute baseline fidelity_score for top 30 probes (action: runbook task OBS-AUDIT-01).
  2) implement the fidelity_score sidecar in the telemetry pipeline (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/302).
  3) ship dashboard helper that surfaces the fidelity_score and estimated cost (Q1 sprint).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to validate schema_completeness automatically vs manual owner input? Proposal: basic auto-detection + owner flag to override.
- Should we expose fidelity_score to customer teams? Risk: confusion vs benefit: helps teams prioritize instrumentation. Start private-alpha with Solutions Eng.
- Cost model: we approximate, but need an SRE+FinOps review to calibrate per-region price differences.

Quick checklist for probe onboarding (new probe template):
- [ ] Owner assigned and base_owner_priority set
- [ ] Schema fields validated (session_id, tenant_id, model_id)
- [ ] Expected coverage target (pct) recorded
- [ ] Cost_sensitivity label set (low/medium/high)
- [ ] Initial sample_rate configured and verified on staging
- [ ] Dashboard tile skeleton created with fidelity and cost metadata

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Aisha: run baseline audit for the top 30 probes (OBS-AUDIT-01) — due 2026-01-22
- Ethan: prototype fidelity_score computation in telemetry pipeline, draft PR by 2026-01-28
- Sofia: add UI wireframe for fidelity badges and tile ordering to Figma, share on 2026-01-25
- Liam: coordinate FinOps check-in to validate cost estimates (JIRA-OBS-1189)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a probe "trust age" metric: how long since last owner validation; reduce fidelity if > 90 days.
- For rollback playbooks, surface probes with high weight first in incident channel and include quick links to increase trace sample rates per-tenant.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-4521 (telemetry ontology)
- GitHub: observability repo (PR above)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1189 (cost calibration)

Appendix: example panel metadata JSON (intended as text blob for the dashboard API):
- title: "kv_cache_hit_rate - model-a shard-3"
- metric: kv_cache_hit_rate
- owner: "core-serving-team"
- fidelity_score: "72"
- sample_rate: "0.12"
- estimated_cost_label: "medium"
- definitions: "kv_hits / kv_lookups, 5m rollup"

End of note.
